top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: Russian drones struck a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih on Friday, then struck it again half an hour later, killing at least 16 people and wounding more than 130. The Iran standoff turned into a race between exits: Iran's president said it was time to end the war from a position of strength, while Washington readies sanctions on Aug 24 that the US Treasury secretary says are meant to bring the government down. Legal and regulatory pressure ran through the rest of the day, most sharply in Turkey's move to have Netanyahu listed by Interpol; nine-figure fines also landed on two of the biggest tech platforms. Watch Aug 24 - the sanctions text will show whether Tehran's exit signal survives contact with it.

stories.headline: Russian 'double-tap' drone strike on Kryvyi Rih shopping centre kills at least 16
stories.summary: Russian drones hit a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih on Aug 21, with a second drone striking about half an hour after the first in what President Volodymyr Zelensky called a deliberate attempt to hit emergency responders. Regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha said at least 16 people were killed and more than 130 wounded, 22 of them children, with nine people preliminarily missing; earlier reports during the day put the toll at 14. Russia's defence ministry has not commented on the shopping centre; a separate drone strike in Mykolaiv killed four people, including three children, Ukrainian state media said.

stories.headline: Iran's president says it is time to end the war as Washington readies its harshest sanctions
stories.summary: President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran should end the war 'while we are in a position of power and dignity' - the clearest exit signal yet from Iran's civilian leadership. It came as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent promised on Aug 24 to detail sanctions he says are meant to collapse the Iranian government; Iran's armed forces chief of staff, Major-General Ali Abdollahi, said the response would be 'crushing, punishing and devastating' across land, sea, air and cyberspace, according to Iranian media. China said sanctions and pressure are not a solution and urged a political settlement.

stories.headline: NATO facilitates Strait of Hormuz talks but says it is not a NATO mission
stories.summary: NATO's supreme allied commander, US Air Force General Alexus Grynkewich, hosted a chiefs-of-defence videoconference on Aug 19 to help interested allies coordinate contributions to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, his spokesperson said - stressing this is not an alliance operation. France and Britain have been building a coalition of roughly a dozen countries to guarantee safe passage once the conflict eases; the strait carried about a fifth of all traded oil before February.

stories.headline: UK, Canada and Australia call Israel's refusal to open a criminal probe into aid worker killings 'shameful'
stories.summary: The three governments issued a joint statement over Israel's decision not to open a criminal investigation into the April 2024 strikes on a World Central Kitchen convoy in Gaza that killed seven aid workers - three Britons, a Pole, an Australian, a Canadian and a dual US-Canadian citizen. Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, defended the decision, saying there was 'no criminal intention' and therefore no criminal responsibility.

stories.headline: Turkey to seek an Interpol notice for Netanyahu; Israeli PM calls Erdogan an 'antisemitic dictator'
stories.summary: Turkish prosecutors are moving to seek an international arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over Israel's interception of a Gaza aid flotilla, an accusation Ankara frames as genocide. Netanyahu responded by calling President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an 'antisemitic dictator'. Neither side's characterisation has been tested in court.

stories.headline: Israel re-establishes an evacuated West Bank settlement as protests over expansion grow
stories.summary: Thirty settler families moved into Kadim near Jenin, reversing an evacuation carried out by a previous Israeli government under the 2005 Disengagement Plan, with the finance and justice ministers and the Knesset speaker attending. It follows a joint demand from the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada that Israel drop plans for more than 1,200 homes in the E1 corridor, which the UN says would make a contiguous Palestinian state unviable. All settlements are illegal under international law; Israel disputes this.

stories.headline: TikTok to pay US$400 million to settle US children's privacy case
stories.summary: The US Justice Department and TikTok settled a 2024 lawsuit alleging the app illegally collected data from users under 13 without parental consent, in breach of the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act. TikTok pays US$300 million immediately and a further US$100 million once an order vacating a 2019 FTC consent decree against predecessor Musical.ly is entered; the lawsuit is dismissed with prejudice.

stories.headline: Hong Kong's Tiananmen vigil organisers convicted under the national security law
stories.summary: Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, were found guilty of inciting others to subvert state power over their role organising the city's annual June 4 vigils. Both face up to 10 years in prison, with sentencing to follow; a third defendant, Albert Ho, 74, pleaded guilty in January. Hong Kong banned the vigils in 2020 citing Covid-19 rules and they have never resumed.

stories.headline: One killed, three injured in sword attack at a Swedish high school
stories.summary: Swedish police said one person died and three others were hurt, two of them seriously, in an attack at a high school in Fagersta. Police have not given a motive.

stories.headline: Dutch regulator fines Uber €825 million over automated driver account suspensions
stories.summary: The Netherlands' data protection authority fined Uber €825 million (S$1.2 billion) for deactivating drivers' accounts without telling them, in breach of the EU rule that people should not be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing. The case covers 2020 to 2022 and began with a complaint filed in France, but was heard in the Netherlands because Uber's European headquarters are in Amsterdam. Uber calls the fine disproportionate and will appeal.

stories.headline: Met Office forecasts the biggest El Nino in more than a century
stories.summary: Adam Scaife, head of long-range forecasting at Britain's Met Office, said this year's El Nino is expected to peak at over 3 deg C above the baseline in the tropical eastern Pacific - a level he called unheard of in modern climate records. He warned of severe droughts in South America and the West Pacific and knock-on effects on food security. The forecast is a single national agency's projection, not an observed value.

stories.headline: DR Congo to trial an Ebola vaccine as the UN says the outbreak is growing exponentially
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is rolling out the Ervebo vaccine, with some doses used in a trial to test whether it works against the Bundibugyo species driving the current epidemic - there is no approved vaccine or treatment for that strain. Senior UN Ebola coordinator Julien Harneis said the outbreak is spreading across an area larger than France, that the death toll now tops 2,500, and that about 160 health workers have fallen ill and 43 have died. He said existing funding runs out within weeks.

stories.headline: Trump scales back South Korea drills and signals a fresh meeting with Kim Jong Un
stories.summary: CNA reports President Donald Trump trimmed joint military exercises with Seoul this week while signalling plans to meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un later this year, reviving the summit diplomacy of his first term. Pyongyang has not publicly accepted; South Korea estimates the North now holds up to 120 nuclear warheads.

stories.headline: China and Indonesia agree to deepen military ties and cooperation on minerals, energy and tech
stories.summary: Beijing and Jakarta agreed to expand defence cooperation and work more closely on critical minerals, energy and technology. President Prabowo Subianto has continued to frame Indonesia's approach as a 'free and active' non-aligned foreign policy, saying it will befriend all countries including both China and the United States.

stories.headline: Sarawak shuts nearly 600 schools for two days as haze pushes air quality to 'very unhealthy'
stories.summary: The East Malaysian state ordered two-day closures affecting around 200,000 students after air pollutant index readings hit 'very unhealthy' levels, with smoke drifting from Kalimantan. The same haze has reached Singapore, where MUIS shortened Friday sermons because of the air quality and heat.

stories.headline: Japan protests Russian missile tests near the disputed Kuril Islands
stories.summary: Tokyo lodged a formal protest over Russian missile drills conducted off the islands Japan calls the Northern Territories, held days before an expected visit by President Vladimir Putin. The islands have been under Russian control since 1945 and Japan has never recognised the seizure.

stories.headline: Prince Harry and six others ordered to pay the Daily Mail's publisher £9.5 million
stories.summary: A UK court ordered Prince Harry, Elton John and five other claimants to cover Associated Newspapers' costs after their unlawful-information-gathering case against the Daily Mail's publisher failed, with an initial payment of about £9.5 million (S$16 million).

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: HDB will cut compulsory service fees at assisted-living community care apartments by 18 to 75 per cent from 2027 and open them to buyers from age 55, after three of the five projects launched went undersubscribed. Enforcement filled out the rest of the day: LTA wants authorised exporters rather than owners to be responsible for deregistered cars, after illegal use of them on the roads nearly doubled. Scams were the steady drumbeat, from Apple impersonation calls that drained S$195,000 in crypto in a fortnight to AI-cloned influencers selling eyelashes on TikTok. The talk online ran gentler than the news, mostly to small kindnesses - the elderly wanton mee stallholder shoved over a head-pat is now fielding a queue of well-wishers. PM Wong's National Day Rally is on Sunday evening, with roads around ITE College Central shut all day.

stories.headline: LTA proposes shifting responsibility for deregistered cars to authorised exporters
stories.summary: The Land Transport Authority is consulting on an Authorised Exporter Scheme under which owners who hand a deregistered car to an authorised person would no longer carry disposal obligations, with the exporter having to prove to LTA that the vehicle was properly disposed of. LTA is also considering paying out residual COE and PARF rebates immediately on handover, instead of the four to seven days dealers say they wait now. It follows a rise in deregistered vehicles being driven illegally - 122 cases in the first five months of 2026, close to double the whole of 2024. Feedback closes on Aug 28.

stories.headline: Community care apartment fees to be cut by 18-75% and eligibility age lowered to 55
stories.summary: After three of the five assisted-living HDB projects launched were undersubscribed - the Sengkang project drew only 0.7 applicants per unit - authorities will lower the compulsory monthly basic service package fees by 18 to 75 per cent from 2027 and drop the minimum buyer age from 65 to 55. Community care apartments are a joint MOH, MND and HDB offering pairing senior-friendly flats with care and social services.

stories.headline: National Day Rally on Aug 23: road closures in Ang Mo Kio, speech at 6.45pm
stories.summary: Police said roads and lanes near ITE College Central in Ang Mo Kio - including Ang Mo Kio Drive and slip roads to and from Ang Mo Kio Avenue 5 - will be closed to vehicles from 5am to 11.59pm on Aug 23, with illegally parked vehicles liable to be towed. Prime Minister Lawrence Wong's speech, his third National Day Rally, begins at 6.45pm and will be broadcast on TV, radio and online.

stories.headline: Analysts expect marriage, parenthood and the social contract to lead the Rally agenda
stories.summary: Ahead of Sunday's National Day Rally, analysts told The Straits Times they expect PM Wong to focus on marriage and parenthood support and on Singapore's evolving social compact, alongside cost-of-living and jobs concerns. These are expectations, not a published agenda - the Prime Minister's Office has not previewed the speech.

stories.headline: DBS and POSB digital payments hit by a short disruption before midnight
stories.summary: DBS said at about 11.20pm on Aug 21 that customers using FAST, PayNow and SGQR on digibank and PayLah may be affected, advising them to use cards and ATMs in the meantime. It posted an update just before midnight saying services were back to normal as at 11.34pm, and that deposits remained safe. Downdetector logged a spike in reports from about 10.15pm. It is the bank's third disruption this year, after outages in March and July.

stories.headline: LTA to use AI on existing bus cameras to catch bus-lane offenders and spot road defects
stories.summary: The system, which runs on cameras already fitted to buses, hit an average 90 per cent accuracy in trials. Deployment starts in the fourth quarter of 2026 and is due to cover all bus routes by 2030, flagging vehicles encroaching into bus lanes as well as potholes and other road defects.

stories.headline: Friday sermons at mosques shortened temporarily because of heat and haze
stories.summary: MUIS said it was making 'a small but necessary adjustment' to the Friday sermon as the weather turns hotter and parts of Singapore begin to see haze. The measure is temporary and applies across mosques.

stories.headline: HSA halts sales and recalls a Medicube cream suspected of containing a prohibited dye
stories.summary: The Health Sciences Authority said it worked with the three companies marketing Medicube PDRN Pink Collagen Capsule Cream to suspend sales and recall the product, which is suspected of containing Sudan Red - a dye barred from cosmetics over carcinogenicity and allergy concerns - and has opened an investigation. Hong Kong Customs issued its own warning about the same product on Jul 24. Consumers who bought it are advised to stop using it.

stories.headline: 81 arrested in a four-day islandwide CNB operation; weapons found in a Punggol flat
stories.summary: The Central Narcotics Bureau said 81 suspected drug offenders were arrested and drugs worth more than S$105,500 seized. Katanas and knuckledusters were recovered from a flat in Punggol.

stories.headline: Town council managing agent employee charged over S$220,000 in alleged bribes
stories.summary: Phua Gim Chuan, 63, a senior project manager at EM Services, is accused of agreeing to accept S$220,000 from company directors in connection with contract proposals involving several town councils. Mothership reported that the money was allegedly used to buy a Mercedes-Benz. The charges have not been tested in court.

stories.headline: Man who stabbed a priest during mass at St Joseph's Church jailed and caned
stories.summary: Basnayake Keith Spencer, 38, was sentenced to four years and three months' jail and nine strokes of the cane for stabbing Father Christopher Lee Kwong Heng in the mouth with a partially serrated folding knife during communion at a children's mass in November 2024.

stories.headline: Nearly 10 years' jail and caning for man who abused a six-year-old for 18 hours
stories.summary: The 31-year-old Singaporean was sentenced to nine years and 10 months' jail and caning after abusing primary school pupils he was tutoring. The court heard he beat his youngest victim with a hanger more than 600 times, made the six-year-old hold a push-up position for hours, forced him to drink his own urine and made him sleep in the toilet.

stories.headline: Tradeluxury director charged with money laundering in S$32 million luxury goods scam
stories.summary: The director of Tradeluxury faces money laundering charges in the Tradenation case, while a woman was separately charged with allegedly handling S$35,000 of the proceeds. Thai authorities provisionally seized several properties in June, and Singapore's Commercial Affairs Department is helping victims consolidate claims for possible recovery. None of the allegations has been proven in court.

stories.headline: Apple impersonation scams cost Singapore victims at least S$195,000 in crypto in two weeks
stories.summary: Police said at least five cases have been reported since Aug 7. Victims get a pop-up on their Apple device claiming unauthorised access to their account, then an unsolicited call - often from a +1 North American number - from someone posing as Apple technical support, who extracts the Apple ID, crypto account details and one-time passwords via fake sites such as chat-apple.com. Apple never asks for credentials by call or pop-up; suspicious calls can be reported to the ScamShield Helpline.

stories.headline: CNA dissects how scammers faked a Zoom call featuring PM Wong and other leaders
stories.summary: Analysis of the full footage, shared exclusively with CNA, found the scammers stitched together obscure and dated YouTube clips of high-profile figures with other deceptive techniques to make a fabricated virtual event look convincing. The piece breaks down the tells viewers can look for.

stories.headline: TikTok ads use AI clones of influencer Dewy Choo and actor Zhang Linghe to target Singaporeans
stories.summary: Influencer Dewy Choo, who has close to half a million followers, found her likeness and voice hijacked without consent in a TikTok advertisement selling false eyelashes. Ads from the same anonymous account used AI-generated images of Chinese actor Zhang Linghe placed at East Coast Park and Marina Bay to sell mascara and caps.

stories.headline: Police block a website that falsely claimed links to Singapore's foreign ministry
stories.summary: Singapore police blocked access to a site that falsely represented itself as connected to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. CNA reported that the websites of two other entities describing themselves as a Singapore-headquartered consultancy and think-tank were also no longer accessible.

stories.headline: Government begins beta testing a chatbot to make official information easier to find
stories.summary: GovTech and the Public Service Division said the chatbot is meant to help members of the public reach official information more easily, and stressed it is not a replacement for helplines or for officers who speak with the public.

stories.headline: Four operators cleared to add 200MW of data centre capacity under green energy conditions
stories.summary: Digital Realty, Equinix, Keppel Data Centres and ST Telemedia Global Data Centres were each allocated 50MW, beating more than 16 other proposals in the second Data Centre Call for Application run by EDB and IMDA since Dec 1, 2025. Each has committed to powering more than half the new capacity from green energy sources.

stories.headline: 3,000 lower-income residents in the north-east to get $500 each in warm meal credits
stories.summary: OCBC and the North East CDC launched Warm Meals @ North East on Aug 21, giving 1,000 households in Tampines, Punggol and Pasir Ris-Changi $500 in meal credits each - about 165 meals - redeemable at roughly 30 food lockers at or near HDB rental block void decks. The programme aims to provide 165,000 meals to more than 3,000 residents over a year from September.

stories.headline: Singapore and Vietnam to hold their first strategic dialogue on Aug 25
stories.summary: Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Defence Minister Chan Chun Sing will co-chair the inaugural Singapore-Vietnam Strategic Dialogue with Tran Cam Tu of the Communist Party of Vietnam's Central Committee Secretariat, the Public Service Division said. The agenda covers governance, leadership development, public service transformation and technology cooperation under the two countries' Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

stories.headline: Singaporean man, 56, jailed 14 days and fined in Johor for insulting Islam
stories.summary: Mohamed Anim Atam was sentenced by a Johor court after a video recorded by an e-hailing driver, in which he made remarks about the Quran while travelling in Johor Bahru, circulated online. CNA reported the fine as about US$1,733; Mothership put it at S$2,192.

stories.headline: MOM looking into claim that an airport wheelchair assistant had S$5 docked for being 11 seconds late
stories.summary: The Ministry of Manpower said it has contacted the employer to establish the nature and extent of the deductions after the claim circulated online. The worker is employed through a contractor providing wheelchair assistance at Changi Airport.

stories.headline: YouTube Premium raises prices in Singapore across all subscription plans
stories.summary: YouTube emailed Singapore subscribers to say prices are going up across its Premium plans. The increase affects individual, family and student tiers.

stories.headline: Police appeal for information on a missing 13-year-old girl last seen in Jurong West
stories.summary: The girl was last seen near Westwood Avenue on Aug 19. Anyone with information is asked to contact the police.

stories.headline: Director of firms linked to more than 400 unpaid migrant workers declared bankrupt
stories.summary: A bankruptcy order was made on Aug 13 against Ramu Palani Velu, an Indian national and Singapore permanent resident who directs seven local companies in air-conditioning, plumbing and building works. In June, more than 400 workers from three of them - VVR Plant Engineering, SK Industries and KPA Engineering - lodged claims for unpaid wages, some saying they had gone about three months without salary.

stories.headline: Licensed debt collectors found to have breached the harassment law four times
stories.summary: In grounds of decision released on Aug 19, Protection from Harassment Court Judge Gregory Gan found employees of a licensed debt collection firm breached the Protection from Harassment Act on four occasions while pursuing an alleged private debt - shouting insults and threats at the debtor's home and visiting her husband's workplace to hand staff notices about a debt unrelated to his job. A licence, the judge said, is not 'carte blanche' to break the law.

stories.headline: PUB says the Pandan Reservoir crocodile photo was fake; police report lodged
stories.summary: Water activities at the reservoir were suspended after PUB was alerted to a reported sighting at about 3pm on Aug 20. The agency later said the circulating photo was found to be fake and filed a police report. Residents nearby had already shrugged the report off, telling CNA it was 'nothing special'.

stories.headline: Consumer watchdog warns of 'compensation' phishing e-mails
stories.summary: CASE warned of e-mails promising compensation payouts that are designed to harvest personal and payment details, urging recipients not to click through or share information.

stories.headline: Two Traffic Police officers hospitalised after a vehicle caught fire on the BKE
stories.summary: The officers were taken to hospital for smoke inhalation after a vehicle fire on the Bukit Timah Expressway on Aug 21.

stories.headline: Customers bring gifts and children to the Roxy Square wanton mee uncle after he was shoved
stories.summary: Mr Yeo Song Khoon, the elderly stallholder pushed over after patting a child on the head, has been drawing a stream of well-wishers. One father, 40, brought his daughter specifically to encourage him to keep interacting with young customers. Mr Yeo is mostly seated at his stall and walks unsteadily; his family has said he has had difficulty walking for years.

stories.headline: Beatty Secondary students track down a wallet's owner through his NRIC and return it intact
stories.summary: A TikTok user posted CCTV footage of three students at his door with the wallet and its contents untouched, after finding it on a bus and using the address on his NRIC to locate him. 'Your money also inside, I never steal,' one is heard saying to the camera when nobody answered the door.

stories.headline: Fake Mothership account pushes bogus S$139 Rolex deals
stories.summary: Mothership said readers alerted it to an impersonation account advertising heavily discounted watches, including S$139 Rolexes. The outlet is not offering any watch discounts; the page appears to have been taken down and Mothership says it is working with authorities on other impersonation accounts.

stories.headline: Actor Elvin Ng shares the decision to euthanise his 17-year-old dog
stories.summary: The 45-year-old posted on Instagram on Aug 18 about putting down Bagel, a shelter dog he adopted nine years ago when she was about eight. He wrote that the vet advised it as she was frail and likely in pain, called it 'a very difficult action to take' and said he felt guilty.

stories.headline: Japan Home stores reopen in Singapore under the operator behind Valu$
stories.summary: Parent company IH Retail said all its Singapore stores resumed on Aug 20 after several were found shuttered or closed for stocktaking. An indirect subsidiary signed a three-year master franchise agreement on Aug 13 with Radha Export, which runs the ABC and Valu$ chains; the handover was completed on Aug 19 and Valu$ goods have begun appearing on the shelves.

stories.headline: Blackpink's Jennie: agency says it will sue over a 'maliciously edited' performance clip
stories.summary: OA Entertainment said it will pursue civil and criminal action over malicious online content targeting the singer, vowing 'no settlement or leniency', after an unverified clip from her Summer Sonic 2026 set in Japan spread online. The clip's authenticity has not been established and the account that posted it has been suspended; in South Korea, even viewing non-consensual deepfake material can carry up to three years in prison.

stories.headline: Video of a woman collecting roadside Hungry Ghost offerings sparks debate
stories.summary: Shin Min Daily News reported that a woman who said she was from Sichuan and works as a bus driver in Singapore filmed herself picking up apples and oranges left as festival offerings, saying 'it's not easy to work abroad, we have to save every penny' and that fruit is expensive here. The video has since been deleted.

stories.headline: Passerby raises alarm after a teenage boy is seen injured in an alleged Yishun bullying incident
stories.summary: A woman posted on Facebook that she saw a secondary school boy surrounded by a group at 462A Yishun Avenue 6 at about 6.10pm on Aug 19, with bruises on his leg and broken slippers, appearing weak and giddy. She told Lianhe Zaobao he left with the group anyway when she tried to intervene.

stories.headline: Elderly woman injured in an escalator fall at Yishun's Junction Nine
stories.summary: Lianhe Zaobao reported the fall happened at about 4.45pm on Aug 19 on the escalator from the first to the second floor, and that she is believed to have been pushing a trolley onto it. Footage showed first responders treating her on the halted escalator; she appeared to have hurt her head but remained conscious.

stories.headline: Taiwan deports a Sri Lankan man to Singapore after he used a fake Canadian passport in transit
stories.summary: Taiwan's National Immigration Agency said EVA Air ground staff at Taoyuan International Airport spotted discrepancies in the passport of a man transiting from Singapore to Toronto in mid-August, and officers confirmed it was fraudulent. Singapore's ICA said he had presented his Sri Lankan passport for immigration clearance here.

stories.headline: Singaporean, 46, charged in Johor over a road rage incident is a chicken rice restaurant owner
stories.summary: Mothership identified the man charged in Malaysia with obstructing police and assaulting a 30-year-old Malaysian woman during a Johor road rage incident as the owner of a chicken rice restaurant. The charges have not been tested in court.

stories.headline: Motorcyclist and pillion rider crash while fleeing police in Farrer Road; vape and drugs seized
stories.summary: A 37-year-old rider with a 26-year-old pillion rider crashed after fleeing, and police said vaporisers and drugs were found.

stories.headline: A Michelin-starred dinner that is also a play: Nouri teams up with Checkpoint Theatre
stories.summary: Restaurant Nouri and Checkpoint Theatre have built what CNA calls probably Singapore's first true fusion of fine dining and theatre - a 10-course, three-hour experience in which each course is paired with a chapter of chef Ivan Brehm's own story, with Brehm performing.

stories.headline: Ex-teacher's Chinese-Muslim beef roti shops draw long queues
stories.summary: Ameen Roti's two outlets - a 15-seater at Haji Lane and a takeaway stall at Century Square - are run by a former teacher who brought cooks over from his hometown to make the halal beef and chicken roti.

stories.headline: A Sherlock Holmes murder mystery to solve around Bugis
stories.summary: Hidden has launched A Study In Red, an officially licensed Sherlock Holmes adventure running across Bugis Street, Bugis Junction and Bugis+, mixing real-world exploration with puzzle solving over about 90 minutes.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: A shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih was hit twice within half an hour on Friday, killing at least 16 - the clearest sign yet that Russia's escalation is aimed at cities and the emergency crews who respond to them, not the front line. In the Gulf the fight has moved onto the diplomatic calendar: Iran's president signalled he wants out, while Washington prepares an Aug 24 sanctions package meant to topple the government and NATO's commander quietly convened allies to plan Hormuz escort options he insists are not a NATO mission. The Israeli-Palestinian theatre is being contested through courts and settlement maps rather than battle lines, with Turkey seeking an Interpol notice for Netanyahu. All three theatres are now moving faster inside institutions than on the ground, which means the next fortnight's decisions get made in Brussels, Ankara and The Hague as much as in the field.

theatres.name: Russia-Ukraine War
theatres.status: Russia's air war on cities is where the escalation is, not the front line. A double-tap drone strike on a Kryvyi Rih shopping centre on Aug 21 killed at least 16 and wounded more than 130 including 22 children, with a second drone arriving half an hour after the first; a separate strike in Mykolaiv killed four, three of them children. It followed a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv that killed 17 the day before. Diplomacy is stirring without a track: the French, British and German leaders will co-chair a meeting on Ukraine on Monday, while a senior Russian diplomat says Moscow will weigh new ideas only on its own terms. The pressure runs both ways - the BBC reports petrol shortages spreading inside Russia after months of Ukrainian strikes on refineries - and the espionage front widened with Russian claims of nine arrests and an Australian prosecution of a man accused of informing for Moscow.

timeline.event: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, opening the largest land war in Europe since 1945.
At least 13 people are killed in a Ukrainian drone strike deep inside Russia, according to Russian officials. The claim has not been independently verified.
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia is using North Korean missiles to strike Ukraine. Moscow and Pyongyang have not confirmed the claim.
Major Russian grain export terminals are hit in a Ukrainian attack on a Black Sea port, extending the campaign against Russian export infrastructure.
Russia dismisses the idea of a Black Sea ceasefire, saying it sees no grounds for 'half-measures' that would give the other side a respite.
NATO jets shoot down a drone that entered Latvian airspace, the latest spillover of the air war into alliance territory.
Russia's defence ministry says its summer campaign has resulted in the capture of 19 settlements in southeastern Ukraine. Kyiv has not confirmed the claim.
Ukraine's General Staff says long-range strikes hit the Progress Rocket Space Centre in Samara, some 900km inside Russia, and a military airfield.

Ukrainian drones kill five people in a residential area of Russia's Rostov region and three more in the Belgorod, Kursk and Moscow regions, regional governors say; four others are reported killed in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine. Moscow's regional governor calls it 'one of the most massive drone attacks in recent memory' and Russia's defence ministry says it intercepted 822 drones overnight.

Russian drones and missiles kill two people and wound 14 at ArcelorMittal's steel plant in Kryvyi Rih, which partially halts production, and burn down stalls at Kyiv's Pochaina second-hand book market. Zelensky says Ukrainian cities were hit by more than 1,550 attack drones, nearly 1,560 guided bombs and 62 missiles over the past week, and renews his appeal for air defence.
A Spanish F-18 on NATO air-policing duty shoots down a drone that entered Romanian airspace from Moldova, about 24km north of Galati - the fourth drone downed over Romania this year.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and President Vladimir Putin exchange messages reaffirming bilateral ties to mark Korean Liberation Day.

Six people are killed and four injured, including a 14-year-old, in Ukrainian missile strikes on Russia's Belgorod region overnight, acting governor Alexander Shuvaev says on Telegram. A woman is also killed by a drone strike on a home in the Astrakhan region, its governor says. The claims have not been independently verified.
Russian forces attack port infrastructure in the Izmail district of Ukraine's Odesa region overnight, Ukrainian authorities say.
Ukrainian energy company Naftogaz says Russia attacked its facilities 13 times over the past week.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says the bloc plans its most far-reaching sanctions package against Russia in the autumn, without giving timing or detail.
Documents reported by The Straits Times show Binance gave Russian authorities client details later used to charge a Russian over donations to Ukraine.
Russia's defence ministry says air defences intercepted 205 Ukrainian drones over Russia and Crimea between Sunday night and Monday morning. Kyiv has not commented on the figure.
A separate overnight Russian attack on the Black Sea port city of Odesa damages a civilian vessel and injures four people, Ukrainian authorities say.
Moldova's foreign ministry condemns a violation of its airspace by an unidentified aerial object that later exploded on Moldovan territory. It did not name a country responsible.
Italy's government says it sees no sign of a Russian link to the explosion at the Colleferro munitions plant, pushing back on speculation about sabotage.
A Russian court jails a prominent anti-war opposition politician for 11 years over comments about the war, the independent outlet Mediazona reports.
Moscow warns of 'consequences' after reports that British-made drones were used in strikes on Russian territory. London has not confirmed the reports.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin says 620 Ukrainian drones headed for the Moscow region between Monday evening and 5am and that 180 were downed over the region, in one of the largest attacks on the capital region of the war. Regional governor Andrei Vorobyov says drones hit a Wildberries warehouse and other sites and that three people, including a 10-year-old girl, were injured; Moscow's airports temporarily restricted flights. The figures are Russian officials' account and Kyiv has not commented.

Russia's foreign ministry says the United Kingdom 'will pay' for supplying drones used in strikes on Russian territory, hardening the earlier warning of 'consequences'. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Russia summons Japan's ambassador over the disputed Kuril Islands, which Tokyo calls the Northern Territories. Japan has not detailed its response.
Myanmar's leader Min Aung Hlaing is due in Moscow to meet President Vladimir Putin on his first trip there as president, one of a small number of leaders visiting Russia during the war.

A Russian missile attack kills 10 people in a village in Ukraine's north-eastern Kharkiv region, President Volodymyr Zelensky says, adding that Kyiv will respond. The figure is Ukraine's and has not been independently verified; Moscow has not commented.

A court in Stuttgart convicts a Ukrainian man over what German prosecutors describe as a Russian intelligence-linked plot to detonate parcels in Europe. Moscow has denied involvement in previous parcel-bomb cases.

The IAEA says a drone exploded at a bus stop used by staff of the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, killing one person and injuring several others. Russian officials blame Ukraine and call it one of the most serious incidents at the plant; Kyiv has not commented. The IAEA reports no nuclear safety or security damage.

Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Russia has the right to treat British involvement in strikes on Russian territory as participation in the war, according to Interfax. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham says the United Kingdom 'supports Ukraine 100%' in response to Russia's warning over drones used against Russian territory.

Estonia's prime minister says the country is investigating whether Russia was involved in an arson attack last week on a building housing a defence contractor. No conclusion has been announced and Moscow has not commented.
Ukraine's new defence minister takes office after a parliamentary vote, which the country's anti-corruption agencies had opened a probe ahead of.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, publicly calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge to President Volodymyr Zelensky since the 2022 invasion. Ukraine has not held elections under martial law.

German federal prosecutors say a second suspect in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage investigation has been arrested in Croatia. Prosecutors have not published the suspect's identity or alleged role.
The Straits Times reports that Russia's 'pivot to Asia' is prioritising ties with isolated states over larger economies, as Moscow's options for trade and diplomacy narrow.
Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denies President Volodymyr Zelensky's claim that Pyongyang is deploying additional troops to support Russia. Kyiv has not withdrawn the claim.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine grind to a virtual halt, The Straits Times reports, after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.
A suspected sabotage attack fails to disrupt deliveries by Estonian defence manufacturer Milrem to Ukraine, according to the company. Investigators have not publicly attributed the attempt.

Protests in Kyiv back former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov's call for a wartime presidential election, Al Jazeera reports, turning his statement into the first visible street mobilisation on the question since 2022.
Russia and Ukraine each hand over 103 prisoners of war in an exchange, one of the few channels between the two sides still operating.

Ukrainian officials say at least 15 people were killed and dozens injured in an overnight ballistic-missile and drone attack on Kyiv, with a nine-storey residential block destroyed in Solomianskyi district and a children's hospital, a school and warehouses damaged. The toll was revised upward through the day from an initial five. Moscow has not commented on the toll.

Ukraine's air force says Russia launched dozens of missiles and 168 drones overnight and that most cruise missiles and nearly 90% of the drones were downed, without specifying how many ballistic missiles were fired or intercepted. Officials say Kyiv is effectively defenceless against ballistic missiles because of an acute shortage of interceptors.
timeline.source: Ukrainian Air Force via BBC, NBC News

timeline.event: German prosecutors say a Ukrainian man has been arrested in Croatia over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage, the second arrest in the investigation. Prosecutors have not detailed his alleged role.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge yet to President Volodymyr Zelensky. The Kremlin says the call shows splits in Kyiv.
Poland says it has arrested a man over an alleged plot to assassinate an official in Ukraine's arms industry. Warsaw has not named the suspect or the intended target.
Romania's defence minister says the country destroyed a marine drone near the Neptun Deep gas project in the Black Sea. Bucharest has not attributed the drone to a party.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine remain at a virtual halt after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.

Ukraine's State Emergency Service says at least 17 people were killed and more than 40 injured in the overnight attack on Kyiv, which struck blocks of flats and warehouses and damaged a children's hospital and a school. CNA's earlier count was 16. The figures are Ukrainian and have not been independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Ukraine State Emergency Service)

timeline.event: Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko tells the BBC that critical infrastructure was 'purposefully attacked' for the first time in several months, disrupting hot water supply in parts of the city.
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine urgently needs more Patriot interceptors and that the shortage is costing lives.

A senior Russian diplomat says Moscow is ready to consider new ideas on a Ukraine peace settlement but only on its own conditions, repeating that any talks must recognise the 'new realities on the ground'.
Russia holds a rare missile test near the disputed islands north of Japan that Tokyo calls the Northern Territories.

Australia charges a 27-year-old Russian-Australian citizen with foreign interference, alleging he joined Ukraine's armed forces to gather information on their military activities for Russia. The allegations have not been tested in court.

Russia's FSB says nine people have been arrested for planned attacks and espionage on behalf of Ukraine, according to Russian state agencies. Kyiv has not commented and the claims are not independently verified.
A Ukrainian man wanted over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage is detained in Croatia, the second arrest in the German-led investigation.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, plans a trip to the United States to raise funding for his projects, The Straits Times reports - a sign his domestic challenge to Zelensky has shifted abroad after the wartime-election protests ended.

The BBC's Steve Rosenberg reports petrol shortages spreading in Russia as the cumulative effect of Ukrainian strikes on refineries and export infrastructure reaches ordinary consumers, though he finds little erosion of public support for the war.
Japan lodges a formal protest over Russia's missile test near the disputed Kuril Islands, held days ahead of an expected Putin visit.

Russian drones strike a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih, Zelensky's home city, with a second drone hitting about half an hour after the first. Regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha says at least 16 people were killed and more than 130 wounded, 22 of them children, with 29 in serious condition and nine preliminarily missing; the toll rose through the day from 14. Zelensky calls it 'absolutely cynical and despicable' and a deliberate attempt to hit emergency services.
A separate Russian drone strike in the southern Mykolaiv region kills at least four people, three of them children, and wounds a woman, Ukrainian state media report.
The leaders of France, Britain and Germany announce they will co-chair a meeting on Ukraine on Monday.

Russian state agencies report that nine people have been arrested on suspicion of planning attacks and conducting espionage on Ukraine's behalf. The claim comes from Russian authorities and has not been independently verified.
Russia designates the independent news outlet Mediazona a 'foreign agent'.

German authorities are investigating possible Russian links to a weapons cache discovered in woodland, according to reports cited by the BBC. The investigation is unconfirmed by German officials on the record.

theatres.name: US/Israel-Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
theatres.status: Both capitals are now talking about an exit, from opposite directions. President Masoud Pezeshkian says it is time to end the war 'while we are in a position of power and dignity', while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will publish on Aug 24 a sanctions package he says is meant to collapse the Iranian government. Iran's armed forces chief of staff promises a 'crushing, punishing and devastating' answer across land, sea, air and cyberspace, and China has refused to help isolate Iran's economy - the main practical test of whether the measures bite. On the water, NATO's top commander convened allies on Aug 19 to coordinate Hormuz contributions but insists it is not a NATO mission; France and Britain are building a roughly twelve-country coalition to guarantee safe passage once the conflict eases, which would still need Iranian acquiescence.

timeline.event: Iran says a deal with Oman on the Strait of Hormuz is in its final stages.
Houthis reportedly kill six people in their first deadly attack since the start of the Iran war.
Yemen's internationally recognised government says the Houthis fired six ballistic missiles at the Red Sea port of Mocha, killing four civilians. The Houthis have not commented.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the US will step up economic pressure on Iran, as two more ships are reported attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.
Abu Dhabi National Oil Company says one of its vessels came under attack while transiting the Strait of Hormuz the previous day, according to Emirati state media.
Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi says the strait 'has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian', responding to Trump's threat to declare Hormuz US territory.
Yemen's Mocha port suspends commercial and maritime operations after being hit by more than 25 missiles in Houthi attacks over recent days, the port's management says.
Qatar denies capturing three Iranian pilots, rejecting Tehran's claim that they have been held since Qatari forces downed two Iranian fighter jets.
Iran accuses Qatar of thwarting the investigation into the fate of the three pilots, according to Iranian state-linked media.
Iran's parliament advances a bill further criminalising interviews given to media the state designates as hostile.

Iran's army chief Amir Hatami announces a bounty of about US$30,000 for the killing or capture of US soldiers, saying the plan followed a 'large number of requests' to take part, according to state news agency IRNA.

The US and Iran pass the 60-day deadline set under June's ceasefire memorandum without agreeing a deal on Iran's nuclear programme. Washington has rescinded oil sanctions waivers and reimposed a naval blockade of Iranian ports; Iran keeps the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed.
President Trump threatens to bomb Oman if it 'gets in the way' of a US deal with Iran on the Strait of Hormuz, according to a report carried by CNA.
Iran says it now considers the three missing pilots to be prisoners held in Qatar, saying they went missing during an operation against Al Udeid Air Base. Doha denies holding them.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree says the group attacked a Saudi military ship and four escort vessels off Yemen's Mocha with missiles. Riyadh has not confirmed the claim.
Drones target the office of the Iraqi Kurdistan region's prime minister; no casualties are reported and no group has claimed responsibility.
Iran says two French embassy employees have been barred from returning to the country.

Iran threatens to 'go on the offensive' in the Strait of Hormuz if diplomacy with the United States fails, and says separately it will escalate if Washington does not honour June's memorandum within weeks. The threats are Tehran's own characterisation.
President Trump says Iran will not agree to the deal he believes is needed, and repeats his threat to strike Oman if it obstructs a Hormuz arrangement.
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan urges Trump to pursue talks with Iran and offers Ankara's support in facilitating them.
Government bond yields jump and oil extends gains after the US-Iran ceasefire deadline passes without an agreement, with US stocks having fallen in the previous session on the same combination.

Iranian fishermen begin venturing back into waters near the Strait of Hormuz despite fears of renewed fighting, an early sign of civilian activity returning to the waterway even as it stays effectively closed to commercial traffic.

Iran's chief negotiator, parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, says the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until the United States meets Tehran's conditions under the interim deal signed in June. Washington has not publicly responded to the specific terms.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency says it received a report that a vessel transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an unknown projectile, causing engine-room damage and one crew casualty. No party has claimed the strike.
The United Arab Emirates says its air defences detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran, both of which fell into the sea. Iran's foreign ministry rejects the statement as 'baseless'.

President Donald Trump says talks with Iran are neither taking place nor scheduled and asserts the Strait of Hormuz is open. Iran says the waterway will stay closed until Washington meets the terms of June's interim deal.
Trump posts a map showing the Strait of Hormuz as US territory, days after Iran's deputy foreign minister said the strait 'has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian'.
France says it will expel two Iranian diplomats in the coming days over a July incident involving two staff of the French embassy in Tehran.
The US Justice Department unseals charges against 17 people it links to Iran's Mabna Institute over hacking of US universities, companies and government agencies.

The United Arab Emirates halts all trade and financial dealings with Iran, saying its air defences detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iranian territory and that Tehran has repeatedly targeted its tankers. Iran's foreign ministry rejects the missile allegation as baseless.
Iran warns Gulf countries against assisting the United States militarily, after the UAE's decision to cut trade ties.

The Straits Times reports that the UAE's financial embargo puts the long-standing Abu Dhabi-Tehran rivalry back in the spotlight, with the UAE having been one of Iran's largest trade and re-export partners.
Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz slows further as uncertainty over the waterway's status persists.

The US Justice Department's charges against 17 people it links to Iran's Mabna Institute are reported in full, covering hacking of US universities, companies and government agencies. The defendants are not in US custody.
Iran says its ambassador has met four Iranian nationals detained in Kuwait. Kuwaiti authorities have not commented publicly.
An Iranian academic detained in the United States over an alleged link to the 1979 hostage crisis writes about conditions in US detention, in an account published by the BBC.

President Donald Trump says on Truth Social that the United States is launching 'the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country' against Iran, saying Tehran failed to take the chance to make a deal. No sanctions list has been published.

Trump warns that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities give Iran 'any type of lifeline' will face 'tremendous economic consequences'. The administration has not named which states it means.

The US warns that Siemens programmable logic controllers can be exploited, amid concern that Iranian-linked actors are breaching water treatment plants. CISA has issued advisories; no confirmed compromise of a US utility has been announced.

Analysts tell Al Jazeera that maintenance problems aboard the carrier USS Abraham Lincoln illustrate the limits of sustaining US naval presence through a prolonged Iran conflict. The Navy has not commented on the assessment.

Trump says he will impose tougher economic measures on Iran and warns that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities give Tehran 'any type of lifeline' will face consequences. No sanctions list or named target country has been published.

Iranian officials publicly deride Trump's threat of 'economic warfare'. Separately, Iran's military says it is prepared to conduct offensive strikes as diplomacy with Washington stalls; the statement is Tehran's and has not been independently corroborated.

The Straits Times reports that Iran's practical control over traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is slipping, while the United States is far from having secured the waterway - leaving both sides short of their stated aims.
The US Justice Department charges 17 Iranian nationals linked to the Mabna Institute over an alleged US$3.4 billion theft of academic and corporate data. The defendants are not in US custody.

US agencies including the NSA, CISA, the FBI, the Department of Energy and the EPA warn that attackers are using AI-generated tooling against Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers, with water treatment operators among the concerns.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the coming sanctions will be the toughest in history, will 'squash' Iran's economy and that Washington intends to 'collapse this regime', suggesting the move lessens the need for new major military operations. No details of the measures have been released.
The BBC reports that Iran has for years proved adept at working around punishing sanctions, raising doubts about how much the threatened measures would bite.
The US Treasury issues fresh sanctions on Hezbollah, including re-designating it under a terrorism authority, in a move framed around the group's links to the Iranian government.
A new US aircraft carrier arrives in the Middle East to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has been on station for an extended deployment.
Yemen's Houthis say they targeted a Saudi airport and a Saudi Aramco facility. Saudi authorities have not confirmed any damage and the claim is not independently verified.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian says it is time to end the war: 'It is better that we bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity.' It is the clearest signal yet from Iran's civilian leadership that Tehran wants an exit, and follows its foreign ministry accusing Washington of 'economic terrorism'.

The chief of staff of Iran's armed forces, Major-General Ali Abdollahi, says Tehran will answer new US threats with 'crushing, punishing and devastating responses' across land, sea, air, air defence and cyberspace, according to Iranian media. Parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says Washington appears to have concluded it cannot prevail militarily.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says details of the threatened sanctions package will be published on Aug 24, after saying the measures will be the toughest in history and are intended to collapse the Iranian government.
China says US 'sanctions and pressure' will not resolve the conflict and urges a political solution, rebuffing Washington's request that Beijing help isolate Iran's economy.
A teenager pleads guilty in London over an arson attack on the offices of the Persian-language broadcaster Iran International.

NATO's supreme allied commander, US Air Force General Alexus Grynkewich, hosted a chiefs-of-defence videoconference on Aug 19 to help interested allies coordinate possible contributions to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. His spokesperson stresses it is not a NATO mission; France and Britain have been assembling a coalition of about a dozen countries to guarantee safe passage, which would ultimately need Iranian acquiescence.

President Masoud Pezeshkian says it is time to end the war 'while we are in a position of power and dignity' - the clearest exit signal yet from Iran's civilian leadership, delivered as Washington prepares to publish its sanctions package on Aug 24.

theatres.name: Israel-Gaza & Lebanon
theatres.status: The contest is being fought on land and in law rather than on a front line. Thirty settler families moved into Kadim near Jenin on Aug 20, reversing a 2005 evacuation, and European governments plus Canada demanded Israel drop plans for more than 1,200 homes in the E1 corridor that the UN says would make a contiguous Palestinian state unviable; Israel rejects the criticism. The legal front hardened further: the UK, Canada and Australia called Israel's refusal to open a criminal investigation into the World Central Kitchen killings 'shameful', Turkey moved to seek an Interpol notice for Netanyahu over the Gaza flotilla - drawing an 'antisemitic dictator' retort aimed at Erdogan - and the US-sanctioned ICC president warned of the 'demise of international rule of law'. Strikes and shootings continue, including the reported killing of a Palestinian teenager in the West Bank; casualty accounts come from parties to the conflict and are not independently verified.

timeline.event: Israel strikes south Lebanon after two soldiers are killed by an explosion.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says Israel rejects President Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza.
Palestinians are told to leave homes in the West Bank village of Qusra that Israeli settlers had besieged.
Israeli forces block activists attempting to deliver aid to Palestinian families besieged by settlers at Qusra.
US officials say Washington wants Netanyahu to publicly condemn the settler siege at Qusra. Netanyahu has not commented publicly.

Israeli airstrikes on Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani in southern Lebanon kill at least 11 people, Lebanon's health ministry says, in the deadliest day since the June truce. Israel says the strikes targeted Hezbollah.
A Hamas delegation led by Khalil al-Hayya holds talks with Egypt's intelligence chief in Cairo on a plan for Gaza.
US envoy Jared Kushner meets Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya in Cairo - a rare direct meeting between a senior US official and the group's leadership - while Israel carries out fresh strikes on Gaza.
The Pope calls for an end to violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
Kushner meets Netanyahu in Jerusalem to push Trump's Gaza plan, a day after the Cairo meeting. Israel rejected the plan on 9 August and has not said whether its position has changed.
UNIFIL says Israeli flags placed along a road in southern Lebanon violate UN Security Council Resolution 1701. Israel has not responded publicly.

Kushner's round of talks with Israel and Hamas ends without a breakthrough on Trump's Gaza plan. US officials say Netanyahu and Kushner discussed Hamas handing over weapons under the supervision of an American general, with disarmament possibly beginning within 30 days; Hamas has not publicly accepted disarmament.

An Israeli settler walks onto the land of Loui Ridi, a Palestinian American whose West Bank home in Qusra has been besieged by settlers, in a tense face-to-face confrontation. The Israeli authorities have not commented on the incident.

An Israeli airstrike kills at least six Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, health officials say, a day after Jared Kushner's regional trip ended without advancing Trump's plan to end the war. Israel has not commented on the strike.
A US envoy says Washington is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria to avoid clashes as all three operate in Syrian territory.

The United States sanctions ICC president Tomoko Akane and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye, extending a campaign that began with the court's warrants against Israeli officials over alleged war crimes in Gaza. The ICC says the measures undermine the rule of law.

Syrian state television reports eight Israeli airstrikes on the disused Abu al-Duhur military airfield in Idlib province, saying there were no casualties. Damascus calls the attack an unjustified act of aggression.
US envoy Tom Barrack says Washington is deeply concerned by Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase and calls them an 'unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability'.

Turkey rejects as untenable Israel's claim that it struck the Abu al-Duhur airbase to prevent Turkish forces deploying there. Washington says it is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria.

The Israeli military says it has ordered criminal investigations into the January 2024 killing of five-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza City and into the killings of Palestinian paramedics and rescue workers. Israel had previously said its forces were unaware of the vehicle Hind Rajab was in.

The International Criminal Court calls the US sanctions on its president, Tomoko Akane, and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye a 'flagrant attack' on the tribunal's independence. Japan separately calls the designations 'unfortunate'.
The BBC reports that thousands of people remain missing in Gaza, with recovery and identification work far behind the scale of the task and families still searching for answers.
Syria arrests an Assad-era officer who had fled Austria after being convicted there.

An Israeli airstrike on a Gaza police station kills nine Palestinians, medics say; Al Jazeera reports the strike hit the Gaza City police headquarters and killed the head of the women's police. Israel has not published its account of the target.

Sources tell The Straits Times that the Mossad chief and Syria's foreign minister discussed Turkish military deployments before Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase. Neither government has confirmed the meeting.
Lebanon hands a former Assad-era Syrian army general to Damascus after an arrest warrant, the first such transfer since Assad's fall.

The Israeli military confirms its soldiers fired at the car in which five-year-old Hind Rajab was killed in Gaza City in January 2024, reversing its earlier account, and opens a criminal investigation. Her family says it does not trust the Israeli judiciary.
The United States commits US$206 million towards an international stabilisation force for Gaza, despite its 15-point peace plan remaining deadlocked.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decides not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian World Central Kitchen aid worker in Gaza.

Israel opens bidding for construction in a highly sensitive area of the occupied West Bank; critics say the project would sever the northern West Bank from the south. Britain's foreign minister says he plans sanctions over settlement expansion.
US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee warns Israeli settlers not to take land belonging to Palestinian Americans.
The BBC reports multiple deadly Israeli strikes across Gaza in under 24 hours. Casualty figures are from Gaza health officials and have not been independently verified.

Israel and Turkey step up warnings over Syria after Israel's bombing of the Abu al-Duhur airbase; Syria says no Turkish military build-up is planned there. The Straits Times reports Netanyahu is putting Turkey in Israel's crosshairs as an election approaches.

An Assad-era officer is extradited to Syria to face war crimes charges, the first such extradition since Assad's fall, after Lebanon handed a former Assad-era general to Damascus under an arrest warrant.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times, Al Jazeera

timeline.event: The UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada issue a joint statement demanding Israel withdraw plans for more than 1,200 homes in the E1 area of the occupied West Bank, a day after Israel opened bidding. The UN has said the E1 plan poses an 'existential threat' to a contiguous Palestinian state; Israel rejects the criticism.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decided not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian aid worker in Gaza.

Thirty settler families move into Kadim, outside Jenin in the occupied West Bank, 21 years after a previous Israeli government evacuated it under the 2005 Disengagement Plan; the current government has overturned a 20-year ban on settlement around Jenin. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, the Justice Minister and the Knesset Speaker attend the ceremony. All settlements are illegal under international law; Israel disputes this.
ICC president Tomoko Akane, sanctioned by Washington on Aug 18, warns the measures point towards the 'demise of international rule of law'.

The UK, Canada and Australia issue a joint statement calling 'shameful' Israel's decision not to open a criminal investigation into the April 2024 strikes on a World Central Kitchen convoy that killed seven aid workers. Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, says there was 'no criminal intention' and therefore no criminal responsibility.
Israeli forces shoot dead a Palestinian teenager after settlers entered a West Bank village, according to Palestinian officials. The Israeli military's account has not been reported alongside it.

Turkey says it will seek an Interpol notice for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over Israel's interception of a Gaza aid flotilla, accusing him of genocide. Netanyahu responds by calling President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an 'antisemitic dictator'. Neither characterisation has been tested in court.

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: Congo's Ebola epidemic is outrunning the response: the UN's Ebola coordinator said on Aug 21 that it is growing exponentially across an area larger than France, with about half the deaths coming in the last 20 days and funding weeks from running out. Health workers are both casualties and targets - roughly 160 infected and 43 dead - and DR Congo has begun deploying a vaccine unproven against this strain, so part of the rollout is a trial. Europe's picture is milder but widening, with locally acquired West Nile virus now in 12 countries. Expect the official Ebola count to keep climbing; the practical exposure for readers here is European travel in mosquito season, not central Africa.

outbreaks.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo — Ebola (Bundibugyo virus)
outbreaks.status: PHEIC in force since 17 May 2026; the UN's Ebola coordinator says the epidemic is growing exponentially and outpacing the response
outbreaks.scope_note: Cases and deaths are DRC laboratory-confirmed only, as reported by the DRC health ministry on 20 Aug from data up to 19 Aug and carried in ECDC's Communicable Disease Threats Report for week 34 (published 21 Aug). The country count covers the three countries that have reported confirmed cases across the outbreak — DRC, Uganda (20 cases, 2 deaths; Uganda declared its outbreak over on 28 Jul 2026) and France (1 case) — so the DRC figures shown do not sum to a three-country total. WHO's latest formal Disease Outbreak News (DON615, 14 Aug, data to 12 Aug) puts the cumulative confirmed total at 4,686 cases and 2,186 deaths, DRC 4,665/2,184 with a 46.8% case fatality rate; the newer DRC figures are not yet DON-ratified. UN Ebola coordinator Julien Harneis said on 21 Aug that deaths now top 2,500, that about half occurred in the last 20 days, and that roughly 160 health workers have been infected and 43 have died.

outbreaks.name: Europe — West Nile virus (2026 season)
outbreaks.status: Seasonal transmission expanding; 21 areas affected for the first time this season
outbreaks.scope_note: Locally acquired human infections in the 2026 transmission season. ECDC's week-34 threats report (21 Aug) counts 98 affected areas across 12 countries — Italy 46, Greece 16, Romania 14, France 8, North Macedonia 3, Serbia 3, Spain 3, and one each in Albania, Austria, Germany, Kosovo and the Netherlands — of which 21 are affected for the first time this season. ECDC does not publish an EU/EEA-wide case total in the report; the Italy and Greece counts shown are the two highest national figures as reported by AFP, which also put the area count at 99. A year earlier, 67 areas in nine countries had reported cases by the same point.

stories.headline: DR Congo begins an Ebola vaccine rollout with a trial against the Bundibugyo strain
stories.summary: The Ervebo vaccine protects against the Zaire species of Ebola, but nothing is proven against the Bundibugyo virus driving this outbreak, so some doses are being used in a trial to test whether it works. The rollout comes as WHO warns the epidemic is growing exponentially across northern and eastern DRC.

stories.headline: UN says Congo's Ebola outbreak is spreading exponentially across an area larger than France
stories.summary: Senior UN Ebola coordinator Julien Harneis, speaking from Bunia on Aug 21, said the outbreak is growing faster and wider than the response and that funding runs out within weeks. About 160 health workers have fallen ill and 43 have died, he said, and responders have been attacked by young men, with ambulances burned and health facilities damaged. Congo's 17th Ebola epidemic became the country's largest by case count in late July.

stories.headline: West Nile virus reported in 12 European countries as ECDC urges stronger mosquito control
stories.summary: ECDC said 12 countries have reported locally acquired cases this season - Albania, Austria, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Kosovo, the Netherlands, North Macedonia, Romania, Serbia and Spain - with Italy and Greece the highest at 311 and 157 cases. That is a sharp expansion on the same point last year, when nine countries and 67 areas had reported. There is no vaccine or specific treatment; care is supportive.

stories.headline: ECDC's week-34 threats report tracks Ebola, West Nile, swine flu, dengue, chikungunya and measles
stories.summary: The weekly Communicable Disease Threats Report published on Aug 21 covers 15-21 August and puts DRC's confirmed Ebola total at 5,290 cases and 2,516 deaths as of Aug 19, with Uganda's outbreak declared over on Jul 28 after 20 cases and two deaths. It rates the risk of infection for people in the EU/EEA as very low, and also carries updates on a 341-case multi-country Salmonella Enteritidis ST11 cluster and a measles outbreak linked to a festival in Sweden and Finland.

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: Patch your Entra ID exposure first - Microsoft says a CVSS 10.0 deserialisation flaw, CVE-2026-69836, was exploited in the wild before it fixed the service itself, so there is nothing to install but plenty to audit in your sign-in and privileged-role logs. Three more maximum-severity items landed alongside it, including Cisco fixes for Crosswork and Secure Workload bugs that score a flat 10.0, while CISA gave the exploited TrueConf and Zimbra flaws deadlines as short as three days. The other half of the cycle is the software supply chain, where poisoned Rust crates run their payload at build time - meaning your CI runners, not your servers, are the thing to check. Identity is the pattern under all of it: leaked AWS keys, OAuth abuse and the Entra flaw all end in valid credentials that survive a password reset, so rotate long-lived secrets and review app grants this week.

stories.headline: 14 trojanised npm packages drop a RedC2 4.0 Linux backdoor
stories.summary: Researchers found 14 malicious npm packages delivering a Linux backdoor built on RedC2 4.0, with command-and-control logic the reporting describes as AI-assisted. There is no CVE - the risk is in the dependency itself, so audit recent npm installs and lockfile changes rather than waiting for a patch.

stories.headline: New SynkLoader malware pushed through Microsoft Teams phishing
stories.summary: Attackers are using Microsoft Teams messages to deliver a previously undocumented loader, SynkLoader. Teams-based lures bypass the email controls most organisations lean on, so external-tenant chat restrictions and user reporting paths are the practical mitigations.

stories.headline: Hundreds of leaked AWS keys found giving full control over corporate accounts
stories.summary: Researchers recovered hundreds of live AWS access keys exposed in public artefacts, a portion of them carrying administrative permissions over the whole account. Rotate long-lived keys, move to short-lived credentials and scan repositories and build artefacts for embedded secrets.

stories.headline: Microsoft Defender's own boot-time driver can be turned against security software
stories.summary: Check Point researcher Jiri Vinopal showed that BTR.sys, the Boot-Time Removal driver Defender ships inside MpEngine.dll to finish deleting locked malware after a reboot, can be repurposed as a kernel file and registry primitive - letting an attacker who already has admin rights delete EDR and antivirus components at boot. Check Point says it has seen no real-world abuse, which leaves a window to build detections first.
stories.source: The Hacker News, Check Point Research

stories.headline: CISA orders federal agencies to patch two actively exploited TrueConf Server flaws
stories.summary: Both flaws let an unauthenticated attacker reach TrueConf Server over port 4307/TCP: CVE-2026-72530 (CVSS 9.5) breaks out of the script sandbox, and CVE-2026-72529 (CVSS 9.3) invokes an undocumented method to run arbitrary script. Versions up to 5.3.9, 5.4.9 and 5.5.5 are affected. CISA added both to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Aug 20, with due dates of Aug 23 and Sep 3.

stories.headline: SickKids data breach exposes employee and job applicant information
stories.summary: Toronto's Hospital for Sick Children disclosed a breach affecting employee and job applicant records. Patient care systems were not reported as affected.

stories.headline: Cisco patches nine Crosswork and Secure Workload flaws, several rated CVSS 10.0
stories.summary: Crosswork fixes cover CVE-2026-20030 (SQL injection), CVE-2026-20357 (missing authentication) and CVE-2026-20358 (external control of the file system), all CVSS 10.0, plus CVE-2026-20359 (9.9, insufficient credential protection); Secure Workload's CVE-2026-20315 (10.0) bundles several improper access control issues. Fixed in Crosswork 7.2.1-SP and Secure Workload 3.10.9.1 and 4.0.4.16. Cisco says the bugs were found internally and none is known to be exploited.

stories.headline: GitLab CVE-2026-19478 comes under active exploitation days after disclosure
stories.summary: NVD rates the flaw 9.4 and describes conditions in which an unauthenticated attacker can act against GitLab CE/EE. Affected versions are 18.2 before 18.11.11, 19.0 before 19.0.8, 19.1 before 19.1.6 and 19.2 before 19.2.4 - upgrade immediately if you self-host.

stories.headline: Microsoft Entra ID flaw rated CVSS 10.0 exploited in the wild
stories.summary: Deserialisation of untrusted data in Entra ID allowed an unauthenticated attacker to execute code over the network with no user interaction. Because Entra ID is a Microsoft-run cloud service, Microsoft says it has already mitigated the flaw on its own infrastructure and no customer patch is required - but Microsoft has not said who exploited it, when, or how widely, so identity teams should still review sign-in and privileged-role activity.

stories.headline: Rust supply chain attack plants build-time malware in crates with 245 million downloads
stories.summary: Attackers poisoned Rust crates - BleepingComputer names arrayref among them - so that malicious code runs at build time and drops an infostealer. Because execution happens during cargo build rather than at runtime, CI runners and developer machines are the exposure; pin and audit dependency versions and rotate any credentials those builds could see.

stories.headline: Suspected Russian hackers abuse Google OAuth and WhatsApp device linking to hijack accounts
stories.summary: The campaign walks targets through legitimate OAuth consent and WhatsApp linked-device flows rather than stealing passwords, so the takeover survives password resets. Review linked devices and third-party app grants; MFA alone does not stop this pattern.

stories.headline: AI-generated exploit scripts target Siemens S7 PLCs in US critical infrastructure
stories.summary: Researchers reported exploit scripts aimed at Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers in US critical infrastructure that show signs of AI assistance in their construction. The takeaway for OT operators is exposure, not novelty: S7 controllers should not be reachable from the internet.

stories.headline: Critical Elementor Pro bug lets unauthenticated attackers upload PHP and run code
stories.summary: A mismatch between the validation and processing loops in Elementor Pro's File Upload module lets a crafted multipart request with an empty first filename slip a PHP payload into wp-content/uploads/elementor/forms/. Only sites on 4.2.1 or earlier with a published page containing an Elementor form File Upload field are exposed. Patched in 4.2.2, released Aug 19.

stories.headline: Cryptographic context injection attack could let web pages steal Grok chat data
stories.summary: Researchers described an attack in which a visited web page can induce the AI assistant to leak conversation content, a cross-context leak rather than a server-side bug. Treat browser-integrated assistants as capable of exfiltrating whatever is in their context.

stories.headline: isolated-vm flaw lets sandboxed JavaScript escape to the host
stories.summary: A bug in the isolated-vm Node.js library allows code running inside the sandbox to reach the host process, opening a path to remote code execution. Anyone running untrusted JavaScript through isolated-vm - a common pattern for plugin and AI-tool sandboxes - should update.

stories.headline: Critical NetScaler flaw bypasses authentication on Gateway and AAA servers
stories.summary: An unauthenticated remote attacker can bypass authentication via an alternate path when a NetScaler ADC or Gateway appliance is configured as a Gateway (SSL VPN, ICA Proxy, CVPN or RDP Proxy) or AAA virtual server. Fixed in 14.1-73.32 and 13.1-63.21 and the corresponding FIPS and NDcPP builds. Rapid7 reported no confirmed in-the-wild exploitation as of Aug 19 but advises emergency patching given how quickly Citrix appliances are usually targeted.

stories.headline: Attackers exploit a Zimbra SNMP flaw for unauthenticated remote code execution
stories.summary: The flaw affects Zimbra Collaboration before 10.1.20 when the optional zimbra-snmp package is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled, allowing command injection through improperly sanitised input. CISA added it to the KEV catalog on Aug 21 with a Aug 24 remediation deadline - unusually short.
stories.source: The Hacker News, CISA KEV, NVD

stories.headline: 'Zombie Card' attack can revive expired Visa cards for contactless payments
stories.summary: Researchers showed that expired Visa cards can still be made to transact contactlessly, because expiry is not consistently enforced at the point of the tap. The exposure sits with issuers and acquirers rather than cardholders.

stories.headline: CDN Tsunami attack abuses HTTP/3 translation for up to 350x DoS amplification
stories.summary: Researchers found that the way some CDNs translate between HTTP versions can be abused to amplify traffic by up to 350 times, turning content delivery infrastructure into a denial-of-service amplifier. Mitigation sits with CDN operators.

stories.headline: Manic Android malware exfiltrates data from offline phones via nearby infected devices
stories.summary: Manic relays stolen data through nearby compromised handsets, so a device with no network connection can still leak. It defeats the assumption that air-gapping a phone contains an infection.

stories.headline: CISA warns of hackers exploiting a critical MLflow vulnerability
stories.summary: Prior to MLflow 3.15.0, the unauthenticated POST /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks/{id}/test endpoint can be driven into server-side request forgery. CISA added it to the KEV catalog on Aug 19 with a Sep 2 due date. MLflow servers are frequently exposed internally with no authentication, which is what makes this one bite.

stories.headline: NASA AIT-GUI flaws could let unauthenticated attackers issue spacecraft commands
stories.summary: Flaws in NASA's open-source AIT-GUI ground-system toolkit could allow an unauthenticated attacker to send spacecraft commands. The toolkit is used well beyond NASA, so any operator running it should check exposure.

stories.headline: 40 malicious Firefox extensions pose as Web3 products to steal wallet secrets
stories.summary: The extensions imitate legitimate Web3 tools and harvest seed phrases and private keys. Anyone running browser wallet add-ons should audit what is installed and move funds if a listed extension was used.

stories.headline: Cloudflare Workers Spectre attack leaks a JWT from a co-located worker
stories.summary: Researchers demonstrated a Spectre-class side channel that extracts a JSON Web Token from a neighbouring Cloudflare Worker at about 12 bits per second. The rate is slow, but it undercuts the tenant isolation assumption behind shared serverless platforms.

stories.headline: More than 14,500 Dahua devices compromised via credential attacks and auth bypasses
stories.summary: Attackers combined credential stuffing, authentication bypasses and the devices' peer-to-peer features to take over more than 14,500 Dahua cameras and recorders. Change default credentials and disable P2P remote access.

stories.headline: Critical macOS, SharePoint, vCenter and Microsoft IKE flaws under active exploitation
stories.summary: CISA added four exploited flaws to the KEV catalog on Aug 18 with Aug 21 deadlines: CVE-2026-65400 (Apple macOS improper authentication), CVE-2026-55040 (Microsoft SharePoint weak authentication), CVE-2026-59310 (VMware vCenter path traversal) and CVE-2026-33824 (Microsoft IKE Service Extensions double free). All four are internet-facing or domain-adjacent in most estates - patch first if anything here is still outstanding.

stories.headline: Clop-linked Windchill web shell decrypts credentials and maps engineering data
stories.summary: A web shell tied to the Clop extortion group targets PTC Windchill product lifecycle management servers, decrypting stored credentials and enumerating engineering data - a manufacturing-sector data theft play consistent with Clop's mass-exploitation pattern.
